title: Implement block-recursive trsm/trmm/trtri/trtrm triangular primitives
description:
Block-recursive triangular primitives reducing to `gemm` per Dumas–Pernet §2.1 (algorithms 2.1–2.4). These are the shared building blocks of `inv`, `solve`, `rref`, and characteristic polynomial.

## Operations

```rust
// All take matrix views and operate in-place where the paper permits.
pub fn trsm_upper<F: FiniteField>(a: MatView<F>, b: MatViewMut<F>);   // Upper A, solve AX = B
pub fn trsm_lower<F: FiniteField>(a: MatView<F>, b: MatViewMut<F>);   // Lower A, solve AX = B
pub fn trmm_upper<F: FiniteField>(a: MatView<F>, b: MatViewMut<F>);   // B ← A·B, A upper triangular
pub fn trmm_lower<F: FiniteField>(a: MatView<F>, b: MatViewMut<F>);   // B ← A·B, A lower triangular
pub fn trtri_upper<F: FiniteField>(a: MatViewMut<F>);                 // A ← A⁻¹, A upper triangular
pub fn trtri_lower<F: FiniteField>(a: MatViewMut<F>);                 // A ← A⁻¹, A lower triangular
pub fn trtrm<F: FiniteField>(l: MatViewMut<F>, u: MatView<F>);        // A = U·L written into L-view
```

## Algorithms

- `trsm`: recurse halving the triangular dimension; inner block uses `gemm` (paper alg 2.1).
- `trmm`: recurse halving the triangular dimension; inner block uses `gemm` (alg 2.2).
- `trtri`: recursive inversion with two `trmm` calls (alg 2.3).
- `trtrm`: upper-times-lower, uses `gemm` + recursive `trtrm` (alg 2.4).

## Success criteria

- [hard] All four operations implemented generically over `F: FiniteField`, dispatched through `FieldVec` / `gemm` under the hood.
- [hard] Zero extra allocation beyond the input/output arguments (per paper §2.1 note). Use in-place `MatViewMut` throughout.  > **Amendment (R4, 2026-04-25):** the chain-multiply step in `trtri` (alg 2.3: `-A11 · A12 · A22`) and `trtrm` (alg 2.4: U-L compression) requires ONE scratch `FieldMatrix<F>` per recursion level. This is mathematical (matrix multiply is not associative in-place at the element-granularity that would let us avoid an intermediate buffer), not an API limitation. The `[hard]` zero-allocation contract therefore covers `trsm`/`trmm` only; `trtri` and `trtrm` carry an `[aspirational]` zero-allocation target with the documented `O(log n)` chain-multiply scratch as the architectural exception. The bench at `benches/triangular.rs` measures both paths so the cost is visible. The unit-diagonal `gemm_axpy_into_view_diag` kernel introduced at `matrix.rs:~2612` eliminates the prior bespoke per-cell loop in `trtrm_inner`; that part of the SSOT contract is now met.
- [hard] Property-based tests: for random `A` triangular and random `B`, `trsm(A, B)` then multiply-back equals `B`. Same for all four.
- [hard] Edge cases covered: n = 0, 1, power-of-two boundaries, odd recursion splits, singular upper-triangular blocks (must panic with clear message, not silently return garbage).
- [hard] Benchmarked via criterion at n = 64, 256, 1024 for GF(7), GF(2^31-1), GF(2^8). Benches compiled and runnable under `cargo bench -p gf2-core`.
- [hard] API consistency: triangular primitives have the same naming conventions as the rest of `FieldMatrix`; signature style mirrors existing `BitMatrix` kernel utilities where applicable.
- [hard] Documented at module level with the paper citation and the reduction-to-gemm sketch.
- [aspirational] Crossover to base case (small-n direct code) tuned per field; `TRI_BASE_THRESHOLD` configurable.

## Dependencies

- Dense `FieldMatrix<F>` type (ab791e27) — must have `MatView` / `MatViewMut`.
- Matrix multiplication (d48a3cfd) — `gemm` is the inner kernel.
- Expression-template design (N1) — operator overloads for triangular views must match the broader expression algebra.
